info.name: Operation Golden Keyboard API
info.description:
Hostel-vs-hostel mission competition backend (Django REST Framework).

## Before running
1. Start the backend: `uv run python manage.py runserver`.
2. Create a staff (superuser) account for the staff-only requests, since the public register endpoint can only create regular participants:

   `uv run python manage.py shell -c "from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model; get_user_model().objects.create_superuser('staff_demo', password='StaffPass123!')"`

   (matches the default `staff_username`/`staff_password` environment values -- change both if you use a different account).
3. Import the paired environment (`Operation Golden Keyboard - Local`) and select it.

## Running
Run folders top-to-bottom (or the whole collection via Collection Runner) -- later folders depend on IDs and tokens captured by earlier ones (hostel ids, participant ids, tokens, mission ids). Registration uses timestamp-suffixed usernames/handles so the collection is safe to re-run without unique-constraint collisions; the final Cleanup folder removes the missions it created (participants/users have no delete endpoint, so registered demo accounts accumulate across runs -- harmless, just noisy).

## What this demonstrates
Mission CRUD, hostel/participant APIs, the derived leaderboard, filtering/search/pagination, claim/drop/complete, ownership and staff-only permission failures, expired-mission rejection, and the claim throttle (5/min -> 429).

item.description: MissionActionRateThrottle allows 5 claim/drop/complete calls per minute per user; run this folder (and ideally the whole collection) quickly via Collection Runner so the requests land in the same window. The mission is already cracked by this point, so successful responses are impossible (409) until the throttle itself kicks in and returns 429 -- that transition is what's being demonstrated.
